acceptance: The CLI and the Python API apply one scale rule for `tpcds_obt`, recorded with its reason on this item.
`num_queries` for `tpcds_obt` is 90, after every consumer of the field was checked (CLI listing, MCP, doc-contracts and docs-data exports, test matrices, UAT).
TPC-DS OBT runs end to end on DuckDB at SF 0.01, 0.1 and 1, and at SF 10 if claimed.
A regression test shows the CLI accepts each enabled scale and rejects one outside the rule.
A changelog fragment records the change.
The report gives the accepted rule, per-scale row count, Parquet size and generation time with hardware, the PR number, and the core commit whose site-inputs bundle carries the change.
description:
`benchbox run --benchmark tpcds_obt` rejects every scale factor except 1.0 ("tpcds_obt accepts scale_factor in [1.0]; got 10.0"), and the Python API rejects every scale below 1.0. The restriction looks accidental: the `tpcds_obt` registry block (`default_scale: 1.0`, `scale_options: [1.0]`, `min_scale: 1.0`, `num_queries: 17`) came in with 9f51cc65ee (#590, a bulk metadata shrink with no recorded OBT decision). `validate_scale_factor` special-cases only `tpcds`; `tpcds_obt` is checked against `scale_options`. The project already runs OBT at SF 0.01 through paths that skip the check (`make tpcds-obt-equivalence`, nightly `sql-execution-gate-obt`). `num_queries: 17` is the DataFrame count; the SQL catalog has 90 queries (93 statements, Q14/Q23/Q24 lettered).

The fix lands in core. The site page `BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site: docs/benchmarks/tpc-ds-obt.md` ("Scale Factors" table) is corrected separately once the site-inputs bundle carries the change.
